findings.summary: Mutation matrix row Q2 reports a kill that is structurally impossible, violating spec §5 item 5 ('变异矩阵各行必须是实测，不得写预测…⛔ 不得编造失败现象'). The dev-note states the mutated line is src/tick-run.ts:1527-1529 (production default readResult's `throw` changed to `return []`) and that 'P2 失败侧测试失败'. But the P2 failure-side test (test/g5-triage-read.test.ts:226-260) calls runWrite with an injected `triageSpawnRuntime` whose readResult is a test-local closure that throws its own error; runChannelWrite — the only place the mutated closure at 1521-1530 is constructed — is never entered. The only production-assembly test (test/g5-triage-read.test.ts:539-598) resolves the result on the first read attempt and so never reaches the exhaustion branch. Therefore no test in the suite can observe this mutation, and the reported failure phenomenon cannot have been measured.

Mutation matrix row Q3 likewise reports an unreachable kill. The dev-note names src/tick-run.ts:1521-1529 (`result !== null` changed to `result !== null && result.length > 0`) and claims 'P3 测试失败'. The P3 test (test/g5-triage-read.test.ts:278-311) injects its own `triageSpawnRuntime.readResult`, so the mutated production closure is never constructed; the sole production-assembly test returns two non-empty decisions, so `result.length > 0` stays true and behavior is byte-identical under the mutation. Two of the four required mutation rows thus assert measured failures that cannot occur, which makes the §4 matrix — the package's primary anti-'silent success' control — itself an unverified success claim.

Spec P2 and P3 are unmet on production-assembled deps. P6 states globally that assertions must land on the production-assembled deps and that '⛔ 自建 runtime 注入的用例不算数'. Every P2/P3 test injects opts.triageSpawnRuntime or builds deps directly for runWrite, which takes the injection branch (src/tick-run.ts:807-818) and skips the production assembly at src/tick-run.ts:1506-1531. The single production-assembly test only exercises the success path (result present, non-empty), so the production loud-failure-on-exhaustion branch (src/tick-run.ts:1527-1529) and the empty-decisions-vs-unreadable distinction in the production readResult have zero coverage. The exact regression class this package exists to prevent — a silently-swallowed unreadable result — remains unguarded in production code.

Three 'discriminant' assertions are zero-power self-checks, which spec §4 explicitly calls worse than no check ('零功率检查比没有更坏'). The P2 discriminant builds a runtime with `readResult: async () => []` and asserts the literal `[]` comes back (test/g5-triage-read.test.ts:262-272); the P3 discriminant defines a test-local readResult and asserts it throws (313-323); the P4 discriminant constructs an object literal with `runId: ""` and asserts `report.runId` is `""` (365-375). None of the three can fail for any change to src/, so they provide no discriminating power over the production behavior they nominally cover.

Q1's per-assertion attribution names the wrong test. The mutated line src/tick-run.ts:1521 lives inside runChannelWrite's default runtime, which the P1 tests never reach (the first injects triageSpawnRuntime; the second calls findTriageResult directly on local arrays). The only test that can be killed by Q1 is the production-assembly test at test/g5-triage-read.test.ts:539-598. Spec P8 requires per-assertion attribution, so citing the P1 test misdirects the audit trail even though the mutation is genuinely killed.

Dev-note input_commit still matches none of this attempt's identities. It records f01f31ac353f0099c7fbfada9a4a3158855417ff, which is neither the dispatch input_commit (5f71f156beb0c68a15f4534128372afafc054c75), the target base (4312caebc6c0f3d85c315baf6f7dca82aa5f2755), nor either implementation handoff (be623c20…, 9906c85c…). The Continuous review flagged this field for the second consecutive attempt and it remains unaligned, so the spec §5 item 4 audit-trail requirement is still unsatisfied.

P7's claimed result (26 files / 472 tests vs the 25/458 baseline) is internally consistent with the 14 `it(` blocks I counted in the new test file, but as a read-only reviewer I could not execute vitest and therefore did not independently confirm the green run.
